concepts.title: Differential Equations and Their Order
concepts.definition: An equation that relates a dependent variable to its derivatives is a differential equation; its order is the order of the highest derivative appearing anywhere in it.
concepts.formula: order = the highest derivative order present in the equation
concepts.key_idea: Scan for the tallest derivative; that height is the order.

identify the highest derivative in the equation to get its order

solution_steps.action: List every derivative of the dependent variable in the equation
solution_steps.explain: First, second, third derivatives and so on may all appear.

solution_steps.action: Take the order of the tallest derivative present
solution_steps.explain: That maximum is the order of the equation.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the order is a positive integer
solution_steps.explain: Order is always a positive integer when derivatives appear.

concepts.title: Degree of a Differential Equation
concepts.definition: When the equation is a polynomial in its derivatives, the degree is the power raised on the highest-order derivative; if any derivative sits inside a transcendental function or a non-polynomial expression, the degree is not defined.
concepts.formula: degree = power of the highest order derivative when the equation is polynomial in derivatives
concepts.key_idea: Degree exists only for polynomial-in-derivatives equations; otherwise it is undefined.

solution_steps.action: Test whether every derivative enters polynomially
solution_steps.explain: Derivatives under roots, inside sines or exponentials break polynomiality.

solution_steps.action: If polynomial, read the exponent on the highest-order derivative
solution_steps.explain: That positive integer is the degree.

solution_steps.action: Declare the degree undefined when the test fails
solution_steps.explain: No polynomial degree exists for non-polynomial equations.

concepts.title: General and Particular Solutions
concepts.definition: A solution of a differential equation is a function that satisfies it identically; the family holding as many independent arbitrary constants as the order is the general solution, and fixing those constants yields a particular solution.
concepts.formula: general solution = family with n arbitrary constants for an equation of order n
concepts.key_idea: Arbitrary constants parametrise the solution family; pinning them gives one curve.

solution_steps.action: Solve the equation keeping all arbitrary constants
solution_steps.explain: The general solution describes every solution curve at once.

solution_steps.action: Match the count of independent constants to the order
solution_steps.explain: An order n equation general solution carries n such constants.

solution_steps.action: Substitute given values for the constants to particularise
solution_steps.explain: The fixed-constant member is the particular solution.

concepts.title: Verifying a Candidate Solution by Substitution
concepts.definition: To check that a proposed function solves an equation, differentiate it as many times as the equation demands, substitute the function and its derivatives into the equation, and confirm both sides agree identically.
concepts.formula: substitute y and its derivatives into the equation so that left side equals right side
concepts.key_idea: Differentiate, substitute, and watch both sides collapse to equality.
question_patterns: verify that the given function satisfies the differential equation
show that the proposed solution makes the equation an identity

solution_steps.action: Differentiate the candidate function successively
solution_steps.explain: Produce every derivative order the equation contains.

solution_steps.action: Substitute the derivatives and the function into the equation
solution_steps.explain: Replace y, y-prime, y-double-prime and so on in place.

solution_steps.action: Simplify both sides and confirm equality
solution_steps.explain: Agreement for every x certifies the solution.

concepts.title: Solving by Separation of Variables
concepts.definition: A first order equation whose right side factors into a function of x times a function of y can be rewritten with all y terms on one side and all x terms on the other; integrating both sides then gives the general solution.
concepts.formula: integral of dy over h(y) = integral of g(x) dx plus a constant
concepts.key_idea: Group each variable with its differential, then integrate the two sides apart.
question_patterns: solve the differential equation by separating the variables
find the general solution of the equation with separable variables

solution_steps.action: Factor the right side as g(x) times h(y)
solution_steps.explain: The factorisation certifies the equation as separable.

solution_steps.action: Move the y factor to the dy side and the x factor to the dx side
solution_steps.explain: All y dependence joins dy over h(y); the x part stays as g(x) dx.

solution_steps.action: Integrate both sides and add one constant
solution_steps.explain: The two antiderivatives equal each other, giving the implicit solution.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values and simplify
compute_steps.explain: substitute the given values and simplify: val = 3 * 7 + 9 gives 30

concepts.title: Homogeneous Equations and the y equals vx Substitution
concepts.definition: An equation dy over dx equals F of x and y is homogeneous when F keeps its value if both arguments are scaled, equivalently F depends on the ratio y over x; substituting y equal to v times x converts the equation into a separable one in v and x.
concepts.formula: with y = v*x the equation becomes x * dv/dx = g(v) - v which separates
concepts.key_idea: Scale-homogeneity means only the ratio y over x matters, so substitute y equal to vx.
question_patterns: show that the differential equation is homogeneous and solve it

solution_steps.action: Test F(x, y) under simultaneous scaling of both arguments
solution_steps.explain: If F stays unchanged, it is homogeneous of degree zero.

solution_steps.action: Substitute y = v*x so dy/dx becomes v + x*dv/dx
solution_steps.explain: The equation now involves only v and x.

solution_steps.action: Separate v and x, integrate, and replace v by y over x
solution_steps.explain: The separated integral gives the general solution in the original variables.

concepts.title: First Order Linear Equations and the Integrating Factor
concepts.definition: An equation of the form dy over dx plus P of x times y equals Q of x is linear in y; multiplying through by the integrating factor, the exponential of the integral of P, turns the left side into an exact derivative of the product of y and that factor.
concepts.formula: integrating factor = e to the power integral of P dx and y times it equals integral of Q times it dx plus C
concepts.key_idea: The right multiplier collapses the left side into one exact derivative.
question_patterns: solve the linear differential equation using an integrating factor
find the integrating factor for the equation dy over dx plus P y equals Q

solution_steps.action: Write the equation in standard linear form and read off P and Q
solution_steps.explain: The coefficient of y is P; the free term is Q.

solution_steps.action: Compute the integrating factor as the exponential of the integral of P
solution_steps.explain: This multiplier makes the left side the derivative of y times the factor.

solution_steps.action: Integrate Q times the integrating factor to finish the solution
solution_steps.explain: The product y times the factor equals that integral plus a constant.

compute_steps.action: apply the exponent law to the given powers
compute_steps.explain: apply the exponent law to the given powers: val = 2 ** (3 + 2) gives 32

concepts.title: Integrating Factor and Product Solution for P equal to a Constant over x
concepts.definition: For the linear equation whose coefficient P is a constant divided by x, the integrating factor is x raised to that constant; multiplying through and integrating the right side gives y times the factor as a clean product expression.
concepts.formula: integrating factor = x**coef_p and y * integrating factor = q_const * x**(coef_p + 1)/(coef_p + 1) + const_c
concepts.key_idea: When P is a constant over x, the integrating factor is a pure power of x.

concepts.title: Particular Solution from an Initial Condition for a Constant Rate
concepts.definition: When the derivative equals a constant rate, the general solution is a straight line; passing it through a given point fixes the arbitrary constant as the point's y-value minus the rate times the point's x-value.
concepts.key_idea: Feed the initial point into the general solution to pin the constant.

solution_steps.action: Subtract the accumulated part from the given y-value
solution_steps.explain: What remains is the fixed constant of the particular solution.
